candidates.title: Choose attention mode before menu or HUD topology
candidates.when: A game has entry, live play, local decision menus or result screens that demand different attention distributions
process: Name the phase as entry/gateway, live-scene action, local decision or result/recovery
Mark protected scene/decision regions before placing controls
Use peripheral live controls when continuous world reading matters; use a concentrated task region when an inventory/choice must be inspected
Choose transparent, locally backed, illustrated opaque or full-screen presentation by task, background and continuity requirements
output: A project-specific construction contract and matching screen/state evidence
test: Real camera envelope and named protected regions
Check full task flow separately from aesthetics
exception: A live tactical game can use a central overlay if it preserves the required world information; a deliberately calm cinematic selector can remain scene-dominant
avoid: One generic menu grid or global bottom bar for every genre
Inferring paused gameplay or touch form factor from a still image

Define a content-safe rectangle or mask that excludes ornaments and transparent artwork padding
Anchor header, close/back, list viewport and footer inside the designated face

Use scalable edge/corner treatment or purpose-sized artwork rather than stretching detailed corners indiscriminately

avoid: Treating the bitmap rectangle as all usable text area

process: Width budget equals actual label/glyph/status ink widths plus only existing gaps and left/right safe insets
Height budget includes supported line heights, top/bottom breathing room, rim and any body allowance
For a circle, test label plus timer within its actual usable face, not the full diameter
Let related controls share corner/edge grammar without forcing unrelated lengths
Keep the target and siblings fixed; move only the inner face for a justified depression treatment
Use an original icon only when it improves recognition at the supported size
output: A project-specific construction contract and matching screen/state evidence
test: Shortest/longest real labels and every supported timer/cost/state value
Actual face/ink crop and hit-region trace
exception: A short text-only circle or long centered button can be correct; flat/no-body/no-icon controls are valid when the brief allows them
avoid: Shrinking all labels to preserve a chosen circle
Counting decorative shadow as target size
Applying a source-image diameter as an engine minimum

candidates.title: Reserve geometry and ownership for concurrent task layers
candidates.when: HUD, menu, notification, projected world prompt or independent control groups can coexist
process: Register each layer in shared coordinates
Assign input owner and permitted interruption per combination
Retain necessary live hazard/objective signals; compact/defer lower-priority spectacle
Use shared reservation/reflow instead of independent corner anchoring
Reconcile projected world prompts with screen-space layers; Z-order alone may only choose which task is hidden
Reserve route/subject visibility as well as UI ink and targets
exception: A modal may intentionally conceal nonessential world content
Online/live danger cannot be hidden under an assumed pause
Observing occlusion is not proof of input leakage

candidates.title: Resolve world-specific grammar before polishing
candidates.when: Develop a bounded set of silhouette/material/type variants for the same task; select a combination justified by the world and reading needs, not genre stereotypes.
process: Build a contact sheet using the same labels/state/background
Resolve corner/cap logic, edge/light direction, texture frequency, type ink and action accent
Allocate ornament to identified carriers such as panel edges or title crests
test: Inspect family beside the actual scene at intended scale
Confirm command labels and status remain visually distinct
exception: Preserve an established coherent grammar; do not invent a new art direction for a bounded fix.

candidates.title: Compose from the actual gaze and scene geometry
candidates.when: Protect the task’s spatial region, then group related decisions into one deliberate plane; choose anchors from the actual gaze route and reserved space.
process: Mark threat/path/aim/board bounds on real full-screen captures
Draw scene, decision, status and utility zones at supported aspect ratios
Specify persistent versus replacing layers and reflow based on measured fit
test: No important object or prompt covered
exception: For UI-as-game, the decision plane can fill the screen; a protected empty center is not mandatory.

candidates.title: Design entry→first action as one visual sequence
candidates.when: Put only needed choices before the first commitment; use the same art grammar while changing composition for the active task.
process: Storyboard entry, setup if real, ready/loading, first input, interruption, result and return
Specify which menu artwork/title disappears and which scene/HUD persists
Locate only first-action instruction beside the relevant object/control
test: Record first input through first readable consequence
Inspect each stage for dead-looking empty states and competing hero panels
exception: Some games begin directly in play; do not add a menu or tutorial solely to satisfy the storyboard.

candidates.title: Select material anatomy by role and scene
candidates.when: Use flat/low-relief anatomy for dense or quiet roles; use tactile body/rim only when it carries the chosen world grammar and action rank.
process: Resolve face, rim, body and contact shadow separately
Keep main label ink area quieter than structural edges
Match texture scale, light direction and outline mass across related pieces
Do not decorate every HUD status as an executable control
exception: A deliberately loud arcade menu or diegetic terminal may need strong relief/glow; it still requires legible ink and justified hierarchy.

candidates.title: Make art stretch safely without baking labels
input: Variable label length or responsive width
candidates.when: Preserve structural corners/caps while stretching or tiling the scalable center; keep labels and state markers independent.
process: Mark fixed edges and stretch/tile zones in the asset specification
Choose engine-native 9-slice/Box/Border or separate cap-and-center elements
Define minimum safe face width from actual text and insets
Use the target engine’s sizing mechanism instead of scaling the entire art arbitrarily
test: Longest real label at several widths
No rim/body distortion or text clipping
exception: Plain geometric controls can remain native/code-drawn; 9-slicing is unnecessary if there is nothing to preserve.

candidates.title: Distribute color and detail by information urgency
candidates.when: Spend high contrast/chroma/detail where the player must notice a choice or changed state; isolate those accents with quieter supporting surfaces.
process: Resolve primary/secondary/system/status/state colors from real pairings
Place ornament outside the action’s main ink field
If bright meters are required, build a separating boundary/backing that belongs to the family
test: Priority remains identifiable without relying on hue alone
exception: Multiple simultaneous urgent signals may all be strong; containment and spatial relation then carry rank. Never globally reserve a game’s existing faction color for UI commands.

candidates.title: Fit type from real glyphs and reading distance
candidates.when: Use expressive type where the strings and scale can support it; use reliable text roles for repeated decisions, costs and live information.
process: Resolve font/license/fallback, size, weight, line height, case and numeral handling together
Measure loaded label ink and baseline beside the icon/rim
Set text wrapping and container growth before choosing decorative caps
test: Actual small supported viewport and enlarged text
exception: Display type is not forbidden for action labels; it must survive the actual string, language and size.

candidates.title: Arbitrate HUD, menu and temporary layers
candidates.when: Reduce or relocate a lower-priority competing layer only if essential information and a recovery path remain visible.
process: Record layer bounds, priority, owner, input and restoration rule
Use collapse, reserved space, replacement or queueing deliberately
Keep urgent gameplay state out of the automatic-hide category
test: Restored layer returns to expected state
exception: Chat, narrative or social information may be the current main task; do not automatically shrink it merely because another panel opened.

candidates.title: Treat motion as a constructed state relation
candidates.when: Animate only a named relation: physical press, attention, selection, arrival or removal. Keep settled meaning independently readable.
process: Specify moving part, fixed shell/anchor, start/end geometry and interruption
Resolve timing/easing as project trial values and validate in the runtime
Separate cosmetic render transform from layout and actual hit region
Build before/mid/settled contact sheets and short interaction recordings
test: No accidental occlusion or hit-target instability
No animation-only success or selection meaning
exception: A hover scale can be valid if overlap and hit behavior are deliberately safe; the Flowlab example does not prove its hit region or timing.

candidates.title: Remove copy only after classifying its job
candidates.when: Keep text that supplies a missing rule, condition, consequence or recovery. Remove duplicated labels, scene narration and filler, then reclaim their layout space.
process: Label each sentence as rule/condition/consequence/recovery/identity/duplicate/filler
Move optional depth to a supported help path
Place essential instruction next to the relevant action
Remove fixed empty height or spacing left behind
test: First-action comprehension by a novice where applicable
exception: Explicit pause, end, failure or onboarding text can look obvious to an expert but still prevent a frozen/broken-state misunderstanding.

candidates.title: Verify construction at full-screen and state scale
candidates.when: Approve the whole composition before judging isolated assets; test crops only after fixing the context.
process: Capture matched full screens, component crops and motion/state sequence
Record units, actual viewport/scale/font/scene/state
Separate source tests from render checks and input checks
test: Clipping, hierarchy, optical baselines, texture/corner fidelity, scene fit
State combination, long text, aspect changes, reduced motion
exception: A source-only proposal is allowed but must retain proposal status; a still cannot verify motion or hit behavior.

candidates.title: Stop polish at the declared visual target
candidates.when: Polish the identified relationships until the target is met; do not continually add ornaments to signal effort.
process: Freeze a short acceptance description for contour, material/light, ink alignment and screen fit
Tie every new detail to a carrier or state role
Record remaining defects separately from optional taste changes
test: All target relationships visible in the actual render
No new competing accent or texture noise
exception: A changed art brief or newly discovered scene conflict justifies another iteration; satisfying a checklist does not prove that the user likes the result.
